description: End-to-end JS demo with all negative cases, redacted evidence capture, and docs/TLSNOTARY.md. A runnable Node script drives the full flow: accept an Olea challenge (nonce) -> obtain an MPC-TLS notarized proof bundle (fixture/mock mode for agent verification; the credentialed SP-API-sandbox run via the real sidecar is orchestrator-only and documented, not executed in-workflow) -> normalize to the tlsProof contract (FEAT-001) -> feed responseHash + nonce into the enclave binding path (FEAT-003 shape) -> Olea verifier (FEAT-002) ACCEPTS a valid bundle and REJECTS tampered response, tampered proof, wrong/missing nonce, expired nonce, replayed nonce, wrong notary key, wrong domain. Capture redacted evidence under evidence/tlsnotary/ (no tokens/secrets/real PII). Create NEW docs/TLSNOTARY.md with the collusion rationale (Olea hosts the notary, not Dowsure) and the challenge-nonce vs TLSNotary-handshake-randomness distinction. Depends on FEAT-001/002/003.
steps: Read .agents/tasks/context.json, this file, and the findings of FEAT-001/002/003 FIRST so the demo uses the exact contract/binding/env names.

Add scripts/tlsnotary-e2e-demo.js (CommonJS, Node 24, no new deps): (1) build a challenge object (nonce/requestId/policyVersion/expiry) like index.js issueChallenge produces; (2) load a representative MPC-TLS proof bundle fixture under evidence/tlsnotary/sample-bundle.json (fixture mode — do NOT require the Rust compile or credentials) and normalize it via tls-notary/bundle/normalize-bundle.js; (3) compute the enclave rawPayloadDigest and construct the user_data binding exactly as FEAT-003 defines (nonce + tlsProofHash + rawHash + ...); (4) invoke the Olea tlsnotary-verifier (FEAT-002) + the existing single-use nonce consumption to show ACCEPT; (5) run each negative case by mutating one field and assert the specific reasonCode: tampered response, tampered proof, wrong nonce, missing nonce, expired nonce, replayed nonce (second submit), wrong notary key, wrong domain. Print a clear PASS/FAIL line per case and exit non-zero if any case does not behave as expected.

Add scripts/tlsnotary-e2e-demo.test.js (node:test) that imports the demo's exported runScenarios() and asserts: valid => ACCEPTED; and each negative scenario => REJECTED with its expected reasonCode. This is the agent-verifiable gate (no creds, no Rust compile).

Write redacted evidence under evidence/tlsnotary/: a README.md explaining the evidence set; sample-bundle.json (redacted — x-amz-access-token value removed, no real PII, synthetic order data only); and an e2e-transcript.json (or .md) capturing the ACCEPT + each REJECT reasonCode produced by the demo run. Ensure NO tokens/secrets/real PII appear. Add/confirm gitignore for any raw/credentialed artifacts.

Create docs/TLSNOTARY.md (NEW file only — do not edit any other docs/*.md): architecture of the real MPC-TLS flow (prover path B: external prebuilt tlsn-prover sidecar + standalone Olea-hosted notary-server, decoupled from Nitro); the notary-learns-nothing property; the PRODUCTION TRUST RULE and collusion rationale (the notary MUST be hosted in the VERIFIER's trust domain = Olea, NOT the prover = Dowsure, because prover==notary enables collusion and voids the guarantee); where the pinned notary PUBLIC key lives; the API Gateway+Lambda-is-wrong-for-notary / right-for-verifier+challenge note; the nonce binding design and the explicit distinction between the Olea challenge nonce and TLSNotary's internal handshake randomness; and the one-command reproduce for both the no-cred gate (tls-notary/gate-proof) and the orchestrator's credentialed sandbox run (tls-notary/prover-sidecar real-host mode) with the token redacted from the reveal selection.

Run `node --test scripts/tlsnotary-e2e-demo.test.js` and `node scripts/tlsnotary-e2e-demo.js` and confirm green ACCEPT + all REJECT reasonCodes; then commit locally on branch tlsnotary-mpc-flow (do not push).
Record in findings: the final list of negative cases + their reasonCodes and the evidence file paths, for the reviewer.
acceptance_criteria: scripts/tlsnotary-e2e-demo.js runs in fixture/mock mode with NO credentials and NO Rust compile, printing ACCEPT for the valid bundle and REJECT with the correct reasonCode for every negative case (tampered response, tampered proof, wrong nonce, missing nonce, expired nonce, replayed nonce, wrong notary key, wrong domain).
evidence/tlsnotary/ contains redacted evidence (no tokens/secrets/real PII); sample-bundle.json has the x-amz-access-token value removed.

docs/TLSNOTARY.md exists (new) and states the Olea-hosts-notary collusion rationale, the API-Gateway/Lambda suitability note, the pinned-public-key location, the nonce-vs-handshake-randomness distinction, and the one-command reproduce for the no-cred gate and the orchestrator credentialed run. No other docs/*.md edited.
verification: From the worktree root run `node --test scripts/tlsnotary-e2e-demo.test.js` and `node scripts/tlsnotary-e2e-demo.js`; confirm exit code 0, an ACCEPT, and every negative case rejecting with its reasonCode.

Grep evidence/tlsnotary/ for 'x-amz-access-token' values and confirm only redacted placeholders exist; confirm docs/TLSNOTARY.md is the only docs file added/changed via `git -C <worktree> status --porcelain docs/`.

findings.demo_script: scripts/tlsnotary-e2e-demo.js (CommonJS, Node 24, no new deps). Exports { runScenarios, issueChallenge, loadNormalizedProof, buildEnclaveBinding, buildExpected }. Fixture/mock mode: NO credentials, NO Rust compile. Flow: issueChallenge() (mirrors index.js shape) -> loadNormalizedProof() reads evidence/tlsnotary/sample-bundle.json, sets response_hash=sha256(revealed_recv_preview) and nonce=challenge.nonce, normalizes via tls-notary/bundle/normalize-bundle.js -> buildEnclaveBinding() builds the FEAT-003 7-field user_data binding (requestId,nonce,policyVersion,rawHash,transformedHash,publicKey,tlsProofHash) and canonicalizes it -> verifyGate() runs FEAT-002 validateNonceBinding(challenge,body,now) then verifyTlsNotaryProof(tlsProof,expected) in the SAME order as index.js submitEvidence. main() prints a PASS/FAIL line per case and exits non-zero on any unexpected behaviour.
findings.test_file: scripts/tlsnotary-e2e-demo.test.js (node:test + node:assert/strict). Imports runScenarios() and asserts the valid bundle ACCEPT=SUCCESS, every negative reasonCode, that all 8 negatives are present, and that the enclave user_data binding carries nonce + tlsProofHash with exactly the FEAT-003 seven sorted keys.
evidence_paths: evidence/tlsnotary/sample-bundle.json (redacted: x-amz-access-token value replaced with <redacted> marker; response_hash/nonce are demo-bound placeholders; request_commitment is a real sha256 64-hex; notary_pub_key_id is an example-shape P-256 id; synthetic order data only)
evidence/tlsnotary/e2e-transcript.json (ACCEPT + each REJECT reasonCode; synthetic illustrative nonce)
evidence/tlsnotary/.gitignore (commits only the 4 redacted files; blocks raw-*/*-raw.json/*.token/*-credentialed.*)
findings.docs: docs/TLSNOTARY.md (NEW; only docs file changed). Covers prover path B architecture (decoupled from Nitro), notary-learns-nothing, the PRODUCTION TRUST RULE + collusion rationale (Olea hosts the notary, not Dowsure), pinned PUBLIC key location (tls-notary/notary-server/notary-key-id.txt + notary.pub + OLEA_NOTARY_PUBKEY env / expected.notaryPubKeyId), API-Gateway/Lambda-wrong-for-notary / right-for-verifier+challenge, the Olea-challenge-nonce vs TLSNotary-handshake-randomness distinction, and the one-command reproduce for 6a the no-cred JS gate, 6b the no-cred Rust MPC gate (tls-notary/gate-proof), and 6c the orchestrator credentialed sidecar sandbox run with the token redacted from the reveal selection.
findings.verification_run: node --test scripts/tlsnotary-e2e-demo.test.js => 11/11 pass (exit 0). node scripts/tlsnotary-e2e-demo.js => 1 ACCEPT + 8 REJECT reasonCodes, exit 0. Token scan of evidence/tlsnotary/ finds only <redacted> markers and doc references; Atza|Bearer|eyJ scan finds nothing. git status --porcelain docs/ shows only docs/TLSNOTARY.md. No sam/mocks/** or coordinator edits; integration only via the tlsProof seam. The nitro-enclave/target/** entries in git status are pre-existing FEAT-003 Maven build artifacts, not FEAT-004 changes, and were not staged.
